judgment.rationale: Both are P3 Knowledge Objectives (same statement-type grain) under the merged Topic Area 'Measurement', but in different sub-topic strands: first is 'Identify the greatest and the lowest unit of mass measurements from kg up to g' (Sub-Topic Area: Mass Measurements, Unit 6), second is 'Understand the comparison and relationship among length measurements from km to mm' (Sub-Topic Area: Length Measurements, Unit 5). Their substantive coherence is the shared conceptual idea of ordering and relating metric units within a unit hierarchy (kg→g, km→mm), so knowledge of one strand meaningfully reinforces the other as a parallel application of metric unit structure. Both share canonical Grade coordinate P3 (rank 2, gap 0) and the evidence gives no substantive ground that either objective is developmentally required for or extends the other — mass and length unit hierarchies are taught as complementary, not sequenced, and source/unit ordering is not semantic. Token/trigram overlap is largely generic ('the','from','to','measurements'), so it nominates rather than establishes direction. Endpoint source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both endpoints plus ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context (merged P3 Grade and Measurement Topic Area headers), which limits confidence in any stronger developmental claim but does not undermine the parallel-concept coherence visible in the full objective texts.

judgment.rationale: Both are same-grain Key Unit Competences at the same P3 coordinate (rank 2) under the same Sub-Topic Area 'Whole Numbers' / Topic Area 'Numbers and Operations', but in different Units: the second is Unit 1 'Numbers from 0 to 2000' (count, read, write, compare, order, add, subtract, multiply, divide numbers 0-2000), while the first is Unit 3 'Numbers from 0 to 10000' and adds decompose and expand over a substantially larger number range. This is a pair-specific substantive extension of the same whole-number skill set to a wider range with additional place-value operations, so fluency with numbers to 2000 supports success with numbers to 10000; the same-rank direction is grounded in the range/complexity increase and the Unit 1 to Unit 3 within-grade sequence rather than wording overlap alone.
